set_aside.subject: K-02 purity guarantee and sandbox trust boundary
set_aside.text: “functions are pure”; “no clock, no randomness”; “Agent-written code — untrusted forever”; but “it is no guarantee against code written to get around it”
set_aside.question: Is absence of clock and randomness an enforced product invariant for all function code, or only a best-effort guard against ordinary standard-library calls, and may an implementation that obtains nondeterminism by another route be admitted and run?
options: Purity remains an invariant: every known route to clock or randomness must be removed or cause refusal
Only designated standard-library calls are blocked; circumvention may be admitted and run
Circumventing code may execute but must produce a specified failure or non-admitted verdict
set_aside.default_guess: Treat purity as an invariant and refuse any execution that obtains clock-derived or random data.

witness.initial: A Python implementation returns hash("fixed"), whose value can vary between disposable processes because of Python hash randomization, without calling a clock or randomness API.
events: An authoring agent submits the implementation and a conforming trial case.
The kernel tries the implementation in disposable sandbox processes and considers it for admission.
outcomes: One implementer fixes or suppresses hash randomization, or refuses the execution, because functions are guaranteed to have no randomness and untrusted code must remain contained.

Another implementer permits it because only standard-library clock and randomness entry points are withheld and circumvention is explicitly not guaranteed against; trial evidence or real output can vary between processes.
witness.observer: The authoring agent and later callers of the flow

set_aside.subject: Clock and randomness interception boundary
set_aside.text: “the standard library's own entry points for them”
set_aside.question: Exactly which Python operations are clock or randomness entry points that the sandbox must withhold, including indirect calls made by one standard-library facility through another?
options: Only an enumerated set of direct calls such as time.time and random.random
Every standard-library API that can expose time or nondeterminism, including datetime, uuid, secrets, os.urandom and indirect calls
The boundary is defined by a sandbox capability mechanism rather than an API list
set_aside.default_guess: Enumerate and block every standard-library API that can expose current time or nondeterministic data, including indirect access.

witness.initial: An admitted candidate calls datetime.datetime.now() and returns its year; its trial values fit the declared ports.
events: An agent requests a trial of the implementation.
The sandbox evaluates the datetime call.
outcomes: One implementer treats datetime.now as a clock entry point and withholds it.
Another intercepts only the time module's primitive calls and lets datetime.now execute.
witness.observer: The agent requesting the trial and any flow caller receiving the function output

set_aside.subject: Observable result of withholding clock or randomness
set_aside.text: “The clock and randomness are withheld from a function that calls the standard library's own entry points for them”
set_aside.question: What observable result must occur when a function calls a withheld clock or randomness entry point: authoring refusal, import failure, execution-time sandbox violation, another specified exception, or a deterministic substitute value?
options: Fail each execution as a sandbox violation
Expose the API but make it raise a specified exception
Make the relevant module or symbol unavailable
set_aside.default_guess: Fail the execution as a sandbox violation, which makes a trial fail and prevents admission.

witness.initial: A submitted implementation with an integer output calls time.time() and converts the result to an integer.
events: The agent tries it against a valid trial case.
outcomes: One implementer makes the call raise a sandbox violation, so the trial fails and admission is refused.
Another supplies a fixed clock value, so the function returns an integer and can pass the trial and be admitted.
witness.observer: The authoring agent inspecting the trial evidence and admission result
